title: KV cache + attention kernel seqlen edge-case debug scratchpad (12)
content:
Context:
Working scratchpad for reproducing/diagnosing sequence-length edge-case when using KV cache + attention kernel switching (fused vs naive) on serving-runtime v0.9.2. Intermittent regression observed in production (canary) where requests with long prefix + short suffix trigger incorrect attention outputs / occasional OOB reads in attention kernel.

Owner: Riley Chen
Quick notes: this doc collects commands tried, error snippets, ad-hoc hypotheses, and next experiments. Informal - notes to self and whoever picks this up.

Repro summary (high level):
- Model: rwd/llama-13b-quant (registered in model catalog)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v0.9.2 (container image tagged: rwd-runtime:0.9.2)
- Config: kv_cache enabled; dynamic batching enabled; attention kernel policy: auto (prefers fused when seq_len < 2048), fallback to naive for some shapes
- Trigger: request where cumulative prefix tokens ~1900 and then a short generation request (<= 128) sometimes produces mismatched logits relative to baseline (no-kv or kernel forced to naive)

Reproduction steps I used locally:
1) Start local runtime with same config
   export MODEL=rwd/llama-13b-quant
   export RUNTIME_IMAGE=rwd-runtime:0.9.2
   ./scripts/run_local_runtime.sh --image $RUNTIME_IMAGE --model $MODEL --enable-kv --dynamic-batching

2) Minimal client reproducer (python):
   from rwd_client import RedwoodClient
   c = RedwoodClient(endpoint="http://localhost:8080")
   prefix = "<long prefix text>" * 50  # ~1900 tokens in our tokenization
   # step 1: warmup call to build kv cache
   r1 = c.generate(model="$MODEL", prompt=prefix, max_tokens=0, return_kv=True)
   # step 2: subsequent short generation using cached kv
   r2 = c.generate(model="$MODEL", prompt="Short followup", max_tokens=32, kv_cache_id=r1.kv_id)

3) curl example used to exercise kernels / perf paths:
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -d '{"model":"rwd/llama-13b-quant","prompt":"<long prefix>\nShort followup","max_tokens":32,"kv_cache":true}'

Commands/flags tried (debug runs):
- RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./runtime --kernel-trace
- ./runtime --force-attn-kernel=fused
- ./runtime --force-attn-kernel=naive
- pytest tests/serving/test_kv_cache.py::test_seqlen_edgecase -k long_prefix
- perf record -g -p <pid> -- sleep 10; perf script | FlameGraph

Observed behaviors / error snippets:
- Intermittent incorrect token logits: top-1 token diverged from naive kernel baseline. Divergence appears when prefix length is near kernel-switch threshold.
- Rare crash stack trace (gdb backtrace):
  #0  0x00007f8a2b2e3b1a in fused_attn_kernel::compute (args=0x7f8a...) at fused_attn.cu:412
  #1  0x00007f8a2b2e9d7c in runtime::execute_attention (ctx=0x...) at attention.cpp:289
  #2  0x00007f8a2b2ec102 in runtime::dispatch_op (op=...) at runtime.cpp:1124
  #3  0x00007f8a2b2f003b in worker::process_request () at worker.cpp:76
  (note: line numbers approximate due to strip)
- Kernel assertion occasionally: 'kv_index < kv_capacity' triggered in fused_attn.cu:assert
- Log excerpt when mismatch happens:
  [2025-01-09 14:03:12.123] DEBUG kernel-switch: selected fused for attn (seq_len=1912, batch=1)
  [2025-01-09 14:03:12.127] DEBUG kv: attaching kv_id=abc123 size=1912
  [2025-01-09 14:03:12.129] DEBUG fused_attn: compute QK with offset=0, kv_offset=0
  [2025-01-09 14:03:12.135] ERROR fused_attn: kv access out of range: idx=1916 >= capacity=1912

Things tried and results:
- Force naive kernel: divergence disappears. (good signal: kernel-specific bug)
- Disable dynamic batching: reduces incidence (maybe batch shapes + packing edge triggers)
- Force fused kernel + run with sanitizer: reproduced assert reliably on debug build
- Run with batch size 2 (one short + one long): failure more common - suggests batching interactions
- Try lower max_seq_len in model config (2048 -> 2040): failure rate drops (hmm that's surprising)
- Inspect kv write code: found suspicious index computation in append_kv_batch when batch_has_padding -> computed global_kv_pos += seq_len_per_sample inconsistent across samples

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV index miscompute when attention kernel fused uses a flattened indexing scheme and we combine multiple samples with different seq_lens (padding/truncation). If we use the per-batch prefix length instead of per-sample prefix, index can go out of range.
2) Kernel-switch threshold rounding (seq_len boundary) uses an inclusive check; when seq_len == threshold and kv capacity equals threshold, an off-by-one in capacity allocation occurs.
3) KV cache eviction/compaction race with background async compaction thread when dynamic batching merges requests. Race leads to stale capacity value observed by kernel.
4) CUDA kernel shared memory layout assumption violated for certain seq_len%warp_size patterns - leads to OOB reads in fused kernel only.
5) Bad interaction with quantized layout: per-token key size padding different for fused kernel and naive kernel, mismatch in KV element stride.

Quick code locations to check:
- serving-runtime/src/kv_cache.cpp -> append_kv_batch, compute_global_kv_index
- serving-runtime/src/attention/fused_attn.cu -> index calculation, assert checks
- serving-runtime/src/batching/packer.cpp -> pack_batch_for_kernel
- runtime config logic: kernel_switch_policy.cpp -> threshold math

Immediate next experiments to run (ordered):
- Add logging to append_kv_batch to emit per-sample seq_len, per-sample kv_offset before and after append (also emit batch_id and packer decisions). Re-run failing repro and capture logs.
- Add an assertion in CPU side path: for each computed global_kv_index ensure < kv_capacity; if not, dump the per-sample offsets + shapes. This will help root cause quickly.
- Create minimized reproducer that constructs kv buffers and simulates fused kernel indexing on CPU for varied seq_len batches (batch sizes 1-4) to validate indexing math outside CUDA.
- Run combined test matrix: kernel=fused/naive x batching=on/off x batch_size in [1,2,4] x prefix_len in [1900,1912,1916,1920] to map failure surface.
- Add unit test for packer that asserts proper offsets for mixed seq_len batches (padding case)
- Instrument kernel_switch thresholds to log the exact float/integer boundary decisions when seq_len near threshold.

Breadcrumbs / related docs:
- existing scratchpads: users/kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-11.json (likely predecessor)
- stack: confluence:INF-312 (investigation doc placeholder)
- jira:SRV-789 (incident for canary divergence)
- github:repo/rwd-runtime/pull/412 (previous kernel-switch tweak)

Notes / rambling:
- The fact forcing naive kernel eliminates the bug strongly indicates fused kernel indexing/layout issue. But batching/packer interactions make it plausible the CPU path that computes offsets is at fault.
- Lowering model max_seq_len affecting failure rate suggests capacity allocation rounding (we create arrays sized to max_seq_len aligned to 64/128). If fused kernel uses packed layout assuming alignment, mismatch could occur if CPU-side capacity uses a slightly different alignment.
- If this is real, it might have been introduced along with the packer changes that optimized for fewer memcpy by reusing a combined KV buffer. Check PR history around packer and kv_cache refactor (PRs in Nov-Dec 2024).

Action items (assignable):
- Riley: add per-sample kv offset logging + assertion in append_kv_batch (today)
- Marina Lopez: create minimized CPU-side repro of fused kernel indexing (tomorrow)
- Devon Patel: run full failure matrix on canary cluster and collect kernel debug logs (this week)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there any path where kv_capacity may be computed lazily and observed stale across threads? (check async compaction/eviction code)
- Are different quantized model variants using different per-key strides? Need to verify model metadata/key_stride is passed consistently to fused kernel.
- If we find off-by-one capacity math, should we roll a hotfix that changes kernel-switch threshold to prefer naive until fixed? Trade-off: perf vs correctness.

References / useful commands:
- grep -n 'append_kv_batch' -R serving-runtime/ | sed -n '1,120p'
- git log --oneline --decorate --graph -- serving-runtime/src/batching | sed -n '1,50p'
- reproduce run with kernel trace: RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./runtime --kernel-trace > kernel-trace.log 2>&1

Last tested: 2025-01-12
Status: draft / in-progress

If you pick this up, ping #eng-serving-runtime and @riley.chen. Attach full kernel-trace.log when posting to the Jira ticket SRV-789.
